title: How to Make a Habit Irresistible
coreMove: Pair a needed action with anticipation so the cue begins to pull instead of merely remind.
sourcePressure: Cues become powerful not only when they are visible, but when they are linked to craving, anticipation, and attractive association.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Confusing attraction with visible reminders or generic enthusiasm.

hook: starting with a definition of craving
counterintuition: the problem is not motivation alone

exampleSpecs.domain: a dental resident pairing chart review with the first sip of a favorite mint tea
exampleSpecs.audience: a resident who avoids pre-round charting
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether anticipation attaches to the needed task
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the kettle clicks off only after the first chart opens, so the cue carries a small pull
exampleSpecs.firstImage: steam rising from a glass teapot beside a chart screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal pool lifeguard saving the best playlist for lane-line setup
exampleSpecs.audience: a lifeguard who dreads the cold morning deck
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the attractive sound makes setup feel like the start of something wanted
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she presses play only after clipping the first lane line and finds herself looking forward to setup
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a lane-line reel beside a waterproof speaker

exampleSpecs.domain: a tax preparer bundling receipt sorting with a monthly call to a favorite cousin
exampleSpecs.audience: a freelancer who avoids paperwork until panic
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a social reward makes the dull cue desirable
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she opens the receipt envelope as the cousin answers, making sorting the price of the call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a receipt envelope under a ringing phone stand

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum guard studying language flashcards only while walking the sculpture wing
exampleSpecs.audience: a guard on quiet night shifts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether movement and favorite surroundings make repetition attractive
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the first sculpture label becomes the cue for the first card, and the route becomes something he wants
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a marble plinth lit in an empty gallery

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit grant writer reserving fresh stationery for donor thank-you notes
exampleSpecs.audience: a staffer avoiding repetitive gratitude work
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether tactile pleasure helps the response begin
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she may use the heavy paper only after drafting the first note, and the feel pulls her through the opener
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cream stationery stacked beside a donor list

exampleSpecs.domain: a chess club beginner pairing puzzle practice with opening a treasured wooden board
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner bored by digital drills
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cue becomes attractive through a ritual object
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he slides open the wooden board before the puzzle timer, and the sound starts to carry the habit
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding chessboard opening on a library table

skillTargets: create attractive associations without confusing them with rewards
use temptation bundling in realistic settings
recognize weak cues that lack craving

tryThisNowSpec: Pair one needed action with one wanted ritual that begins only after the needed action has started.
